_note: NEW area at v2026-08-25 (#655 response-carried request constraints, #744 path targeting, commit d25cce30 instrument-requirements-via-constraints). No 04-08 equivalent exists; do not merge/dedup against the 04-08 carry-forward register.

rows.requirement: A request_constraints value's `required` array (naming fields required on the constrained object) MUST be non-empty; an empty array applies no constraint
rows.quote: Must be non-empty: an empty array applies no constraint.
rows.notes: request_constraints.json properties.required has minItems 1, matching this description text. New in 08-25 (#655/#744); no 04-08 equivalent (request_constraints did not exist).

rows.requirement: A request_constraints value's `properties` object MUST be non-empty when present; an empty object applies no constraint
rows.quote: Must be non-empty: an empty object applies no constraint.
rows.notes: minProperties 1 on the properties member.

rows.requirement: A request_constraints value's `anyOf` array MUST be non-empty, and each branch (Object Constraint) MUST itself be non-empty
rows.quote: Alternative Object Constraints. The constrained object must satisfy at least one. A branch must be non-empty: an empty branch is satisfied by every object and neutralizes the alternation.
rows.notes: anyOf has minItems 1 and each item carries minProperties 1 in the schema.

rows.requirement: The Constraint Expression grammar is closed: only `required`, `properties`, and `anyOf` are admitted at the Object Constraint position, and only `enum`/`const` at the Value Constraint position
rows.quote: "additionalProperties": false,
rows.notes: constraint_expression.json sets additionalProperties:false; overview/index.md#L232 states this in prose: 'No other member is admitted at either grammar position.'

rows.requirement: A Value Constraint MUST carry `enum`, `const`, or both, and its `enum` (when present) MUST be a non-empty array of unique JSON values
rows.quote: A Value Constraint containing `enum`, `const`, or both.
rows.notes: $defs.value_constraint anyOf requires enum or const; enum has minItems 1 + uniqueItems.

rows.requirement: An instrument_group's `max` MUST be greater than or equal to its `min`
rows.quote: MUST be greater than or equal to `min`.
rows.notes: instrument_group.json is not cross-field-validatable by JSON Schema alone (min/max are independent integer properties); needs a coded check comparing the two values. Shared type: referenced both by available_payment_instrument-style constraint targets and by common/payment_split_payments.json (see SPL area).

rows.requirement: An available_payment_instrument's `constraints` field, when present, MUST be a Constraint Expression whose `properties` keys name members of the `constraint_target` declared by the instrument schema for that entry's `type`; requirements on submitted request data belong in `ucp.request_constraints` instead
rows.quote: Keys in `properties` name members of the `constraint_target` declared by the instrument schema for this `type`. Requirements on submitted request data belong in `ucp.request_constraints` instead.
rows.notes: This is the 'instrument requirements via constraints' mechanism named in the release delta (commit d25cce30 per the hazard table): available_instruments[].constraints reuses the shared Constraint Expression grammar to describe which instrument declarations are on offer, distinct from ucp.request_constraints which governs the next request. No 04-08 equivalent — available_payment_instrument.json had no constraints field at 04-08.

rows.requirement: `ucp.request_constraints` MUST be used only in authoritative operation responses; it has no effect in discovery profiles or operation requests
rows.quote: `ucp.request_constraints` is used only in authoritative operation responses and has no effect in discovery profiles or operation requests.
rows.notes: Wholly new section (## Request Constraints, #655 + #744); no analogous mechanism existed in the 04-08 overview.md.

rows.requirement: A submitted request is valid under Request Constraints only if it satisfies the resolved request schema AND every object selected by Request Constraints satisfies the corresponding Constraint Expression; Request Constraints can only narrow the resolved schema, never make an otherwise-rejected request valid
rows.quote: Request Constraints only narrow the resolved request schema; they cannot make a request valid when that schema rejects it.
rows.notes: Defines the Business's authoritative validation algorithm (overview/index.md L198-209 gives the pseudocode).

rows.requirement: When a Platform performs preflight, it MUST use each chosen value's effective path and complete Constraint Expression (not a partial or approximated form)
rows.quote: For each chosen value, the Platform **MUST** use its effective path and complete Constraint Expression.
rows.notes: Platform-side preflight is optional (MAY, L211) but when performed must be complete.

rows.requirement: The Constraint Expression grammar does not admit a `ucp` member/key
rows.quote: The grammar does not admit `ucp`.
rows.notes: Prose restriction on top of the closed grammar (RC-004); a captured request_constraints value naming `ucp` in required/properties is non-conformant.

rows.requirement: Within a Constraint Expression, sibling members (`required`, `properties`, `anyOf`) at the same Object Constraint position all apply together; `anyOf` does not narrow, override, or replace its siblings, and each `anyOf` branch is evaluated against the same selected object and cannot itself carry `path`
rows.quote: Members present at the same Object Constraint all apply. `anyOf` does not narrow, override, or replace its siblings; the object must satisfy every sibling member and at least one branch.
rows.notes: constraint_expression.json's anyOf items $ref '#' (the grammar itself), which has no `path` property, so a branch carrying `path` is schema-invalid.

rows.requirement: When a Business emits a `path` in a request_constraints value, that `path` MUST be a complete RFC 9535 JSONPath query, and it supersedes the Normalized Path that would otherwise be derived
rows.quote: the Business **MUST** make it a complete RFC 9535 JSONPath query.
rows.notes: Checkable by parsing the emitted `path` string with a conformant RFC 9535 JSONPath parser.

rows.requirement: A Business MUST provide an explicit `path` when the Normalized Path of the structured response object carrying request_constraints does not identify the intended request objects
rows.quote: A Business **MUST** provide an explicit `path` when the Normalized Path of that structured response object does not identify the intended request objects.
rows.notes: Requires judging whether the omitted-path derivation would have matched intent; not mechanically checkable without a reference oracle.

rows.requirement: When a constraint must follow a stable identity into the next request (surviving reorder), the Business MUST use an explicit query that encodes that association, rather than relying on positional correspondence
rows.quote: the Business **MUST** use an explicit query that encodes that association.
rows.notes: See the worked example at overview/index.md#L449-455 (stable-ID path for line_123 surviving reorder).

rows.requirement: A Business that constructs a `path` from data MUST serialize and escape each dynamic value as a valid RFC 9535 literal and MUST NOT use unsafe string concatenation
rows.quote: A Business that constructs a query from data **MUST** serialize and escape each dynamic value as a valid RFC 9535 literal and **MUST NOT** use unsafe string concatenation.
rows.notes: Checkable as a proxy by confirming the emitted path is syntactically valid RFC 9535 and correctly quotes any embedded special characters (e.g. a line-item id containing a quote or bracket).

rows.requirement: Before emitting a request_constraints value, a Business MUST validate the complete value against the shared Request Constraints schema
rows.quote: Before emitting a value, a Business **MUST** validate the complete value against
rows.notes: Directly checkable: any captured request_constraints value must validate against common/types/request_constraints.json. (Quote trimmed before the inline markdown link to keep verbatim match exact.)

rows.requirement: A Platform MUST validate a request_constraints value against the shared Request Constraints schema before using it for preflight
rows.quote: a Platform **MUST** do the same before using that value for preflight;
rows.notes: Platform-side behavior; requires a live Platform under test.

rows.requirement: A Business MUST ensure that Constraint Expressions which can apply to the same object (via overlapping paths) are jointly satisfiable; contradictory requirements on the same property are a Business authoring error
rows.quote: A Business **MUST** ensure expressions that can apply to the same object are jointly satisfiable.
rows.notes: Requires semantic cross-referencing of every emitted request_constraints value against every other value that could select the same object; see the basket-wide + targeted-quantity contradiction example at L454-455.

rows.requirement: When a Business includes ucp.request_constraints in an authoritative response, it MUST emit values conforming to the shared Request Constraints schema, MUST use valid effective paths that select only objects, and MUST enforce every constraint it emits against the next Platform request
rows.quote: The Business **MUST** emit Request Constraints that conform to the shared Request Constraints schema, **MUST** use valid effective paths that select only objects, and **MUST** enforce every constraint it emits against that next request.
rows.notes: The enforcement half is testable end-to-end: capture an emitted request_constraints value, construct a violating next request, and confirm the Business rejects it.

rows.requirement: A Business SHOULD NOT emit Request Constraints for rules that may change before the next request unless it can continue to enforce the advertised constraint
rows.quote: A Business **SHOULD NOT** emit Request Constraints for rules that may change before the next request unless it can continue to enforce the advertised constraint.
rows.notes: Policy judgment call (contrasts with execution-time conditions like inventory/fraud/authorization, which remain governed by messages instead).

rows.requirement: A Platform performing preflight MUST skip a value that is malformed, unsupported, whose path selects a non-object, or that it cannot evaluate within its resource limits, and MUST continue with any other chosen values rather than treat the unavailable value as pass or fail
rows.quote: A Platform performing preflight **MUST** skip the whole unavailable value and continue with any other chosen values.
rows.notes: Platform-side behavior.

rows.requirement: Each authoritative resource response supplies the Request Constraints set for the next request to that resource; the following authoritative response's set replaces the prior set, and omitting request_constraints clears the set
rows.quote: Each authoritative resource response from the Business supplies Request Constraints for the next request to that resource. The authoritative response to that request supplies the constraints for the following request and replaces the prior set. Omission clears the set.
rows.notes: Checkable across two sequential authoritative responses on the same resource.

rows.requirement: Invalid request_constraints values in a new set MUST NOT fall back to preserving stale values from a prior response, and sets MUST NOT be merged by path across responses
rows.quote: Invalid values in the new set do not preserve stale values, and sets are not merged by `path`.
rows.notes: Requires comparing two sequential responses' request_constraints sets.

rows.requirement: A response containing an authoritative resource MUST supply its Request Constraints set even when it reports an application error; a response without an authoritative resource supplies no set
rows.quote: A response without an authoritative resource supplies no Request Constraints set for a following request. A response containing an authoritative resource supplies the set even when it reports an application error.
rows.notes: Checkable by inspecting an error-carrying authoritative response for a request_constraints value.

rows.requirement: Request Constraints add no new outcome or error code; passing schema + Request Constraints validation establishes only schema validity, and the containing operation's existing outcome/error contract (including messages) continues to govern submitted-request and runtime outcomes
rows.quote: Request Constraints add no outcome or error code.
rows.notes: Boundary clarifier: prevents a tester from expecting a new wire status or error taxonomy entry for Request Constraints violations.
